rl.title: RL short test on Ornith 9B: done, it works
rl.intro: Three training steps of 16 attempts each, on Terminal-Bench 2 training tasks in Prime sandboxes. 4 H200 GPUs on Hugging Face ($20/h); 12:14 to 12:56 p.m.
rl.note: The whole loop works: the model runs, the agent works in sandboxes, rewards come back, the trainer updates the weights and the model server picks them up. Three steps can't teach anything, so the rewards just reflect which tasks came up. About $3 per step once warm; ~$18 in all, including three failed starts. Prime still shuts some sandboxes down mid-run (retried).

qwen.title: Qwen3.8-27B on your 3090: speed
qwen.intro: New engine (TensorFold) with a small draft model that guesses several words ahead; the big model checks every guess, so its answers don't change.
qwen.context: Context: now stored in 4 bits (mixed with a fixed rotation first so rare large values don't wreck precision). The window is the model's full 262K tokens, up from 80K this morning; a 132K-token prompt ran with recall right, in 23.8 GB, at full speed (chat 103–114, code 144–147 tok/s). Intelligence check: predictions drift KL 0.002–0.006 from 16-bit, perplexity within 0.5%; 8-bit drifted less (0.0003–0.0008) but only fits 144K.
qwen.next: Not yet run: the 20-problem math test with 4-bit context (13–20 min of GPU, waiting on your OK) and a recall check near 250K. After that: a 3/4-bit mix of the weights for faster decoding.
